title: Goodness After a Nondeterministic Choice
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine, let $C$ be a configuration, let $T$ be a natural number, and let $\mathrm{box}$ and $Q$ be properties of configurations. Suppose $\mathrm{box}(C)$ holds, and that for each choice bit $b$, one step from $C$ under $b$ yields $C_b$, from which all runs of length at most $T$ end in configurations satisfying $\mathrm{box}$, while every run of length exactly $T$ ends in a halted configuration satisfying $Q$. Then all runs from $C$ of length at most $T+1$ end in configurations satisfying $\mathrm{box}$, and every run of length exactly $T+1$ ends in a halted configuration satisfying $Q$.
